title: Patient Check-In and Check-Out

sections.learningObjectives:
- Describe the patient check-in process, including greeting, identity verification, and information updates.
- Describe the patient check-out process, including after-visit summaries, follow-up scheduling, and final payments.
- Explain how to collect and post copayments accurately and confidentially.
- Schedule follow-up appointments and coordinate referrals, tests, and reminders per the provider's order.
- Provide after-visit instructions exactly as directed, escalate questions to licensed staff, and maintain accurate, timely documentation.
sections.eli10:
### Question 1

A good greeting is like a friendly 'hello' at the door of a house; it makes the visitor feel welcome before anything else happens.

### Question 2

When you greet someone, you say hello nicely but don't shout their private business to the whole room.

### Question 3

Before you open the right folder for someone, you make sure you have the right person, just like matching a name to a face before handing over homework.

### Question 4

If someone cannot hear well, you look at them and speak clearly, or write things down, instead of yelling across the room.

### Question 5

Calling someone by the name they like is like using a friend's nickname; it shows you care about who they are.

### Question 6

Standing with open arms and a smile is like giving someone your full attention instead of looking away when they talk to you.

### Question 7

Check-in is like signing in at school: the office makes sure they have the right person and correct information before the day starts.

### Question 8

Updating an address is like changing your home address on a package label so your mail keeps arriving at the right place.

### Question 9

Checking insurance is like checking a coupon before a purchase to see if it works and how much you still need to pay.

### Question 10

An expired insurance card is like an expired coupon; you ask if there's a newer one and check whether it still works.

### Question 11

Being late is like arriving late to a movie; you check with the staff to see if you can still be seated.

### Question 12

A walk-in is like a friend showing up unannounced; you check whether there is room before saying yes.

### Question 13

If someone looks very sick right away, you run to get the doctor instead of finishing paperwork first.

### Question 14

Confirming the pharmacy is like confirming the right delivery address so a package arrives where you want it.

### Question 15

The privacy notice is like reading the rules of a game before you play, so you know how your information will be handled.

### Question 16

A copay is like the small fixed price you pay at the door even though the rest is covered by your ticket.

### Question 17

Collecting the copay is like paying the small entry fee when you arrive, not waiting until after the show.

### Question 18

The copay amount is like the price on a menu; you read it from the plan information instead of guessing.

### Question 19

A receipt is like the paper you get after buying something so you can prove you paid.

### Question 20

If you give $40 for something that costs $25, you get $15 back, just like getting change at a store.

### Question 21

A copay is a flat ticket price, while coinsurance is like splitting the final bill by a percentage.

### Question 22

Posting a payment is like writing a deposit into a bank book so the balance stays correct.

### Question 23

If two price tags disagree, you check the real price instead of guessing or charging extra.

### Question 24

Waiving a fee is like changing the store's price tag; only the person in charge of the rules can decide that.

### Question 25

If the money in the jar does not match your list, you recount and tell the person in charge instead of changing the list.

### Question 26

Check-out is like finishing at a store: you get your receipt, schedule the next step, and make sure nothing is missed.

### Question 27

The after-visit summary is like the notes you take home from class so you remember what to do next.

### Question 28

Providing instructions as directed is like passing along a teacher's exact homework assignment without changing it.

### Question 29

Scheduling the follow-up is like marking the next homework due date on the calendar before you leave class.

### Question 30

Handing off a referral is like giving someone the address and ticket to the next place they need to go.

### Question 31

Checking everything is complete is like making sure you packed all your schoolwork before leaving the classroom.

### Question 32

Checking understanding is like asking a friend to repeat directions so you know they won't get lost.

### Question 33

Helping pick a time is like finding a day that works on a shared calendar instead of just circling any date.

### Question 34

Avoiding double-booking is like making sure two people don't get the same seat on a bus.

### Question 35

Recording the appointment is like writing a full note with the who, when, and why so nothing is forgotten.

### Question 36

Reminders are like an alarm on your phone that helps you not forget an important event.

### Question 37

Scheduling the lab first is like baking the cake before the party so it's ready in time.

### Question 38

Recording a no-show is like noting a student was absent so the teacher knows to follow up.

### Question 39

Scheduling a series is like booking several practice sessions spread out so training happens in the right order.

### Question 40

Instructions come from the person in charge of the care plan, like homework comes from the teacher, not from another student.

### Question 41

Medication questions are like questions only the coach can answer; you send them to the coach instead of guessing.

### Question 42

Giving the right handout is like handing out the exact worksheet the teacher picked, not a different one.

### Question 43

Using an interpreter is like having a translator at a big meeting so everyone understands the plan.

### Question 44

If you don't know the answer, you ask the teacher instead of making one up.

### Question 45

Reminding about fasting is like reminding someone not to eat before a race so the results are accurate.

### Question 46

Writing things down accurately is like keeping a careful diary so everyone knows exactly what happened.

### Question 47

Writing it down right away is like jotting a note the moment you hear it, before you forget.

### Question 48

A legal record is like an official score sheet that must be correct because it may be checked later.

### Question 49

Fixing a mistake is like drawing one neat line through a wrong word and writing the fix, not scribbling it out completely.

### Question 50

Backdating is like writing yesterday's date on today's homework to pretend it was done on time.

### Question 51

Factual notes are like reporting what the referee saw, not adding your own opinion about the player.

### Question 52

Documenting a refusal is like noting that a student declined extra help, without blaming them.

### Question 53

Entering the wrong number is like typing $300 instead of $30 on a price; someone ends up paying the wrong amount.

### Question 54

Changing someone else's notes is like erasing a teammate's answer and writing your own; it breaks trust in the whole record.

### Question 55

Confirming contact preference is like asking whether to text or call so the reminder actually reaches you.

### Question 56

A good sign-in is like a secret list only the office can see, not a poster for everyone.

### Question 57

When two kids share a name, you check the birth date to know which one you mean.

### Question 58

Consent for a child is like needing the right grown-up's permission before a field trip, not just any adult.

### Question 59

Getting records is like checking out your own file with the right permission slip, not just grabbing any folder.

### Question 60

Staying calm with an upset person is like using a quiet voice to help someone who is yelling calm down.

### Question 61

When someone asks if they are very sick, you pass the question to the doctor instead of guessing.

### Question 62

Self-pay is like paying with cash at a store instead of a gift card; you note how they will pay.

### Question 63

Telehealth check-in is like confirming who's on a video call before the lesson starts.

### Question 64

The new-patient packet is like the welcome folder you fill out when you join a new school.

### Question 65

A missing signature is like homework missing a name; you ask the person to sign it, not sign it for them.

### Question 66

Checking a check is like making sure a ticket has the right name and date before you accept it.

### Question 67

An audit trail is like a list that shows exactly who touched a document and when.

### Question 68

20% of $200 is like taking one-fifth of 200, which is 40.

### Question 69

Fixing a missed note is like adding a forgotten detail to your list, labeled 'added later,' instead of pretending you wrote it on time.

### Question 70

Saying something kind and helpful is like opening the door and saying 'come on in.'

### Question 71

Following the schedule template is like using the right-sized box for each item so everything fits.

### Question 72

If someone says they'll stop their medicine, you tell the doctor right away instead of agreeing.

### Question 73

Using a preferred name is like calling a friend by their nickname while their official name stays on the form.

### Question 74

Confirming the appointment is like repeating the plan so both people leave knowing the same time.

### Question 75

Finding a wrong detail is like spotting the wrong address on a package; you flag it and check before sending.

### Question 76

If you don't know when to come back, you ask the person in charge instead of guessing.

### Question 77

Double-checking is like proofreading your work before turning it in so no small mistakes slip through.

### Question 78

Emergency contact info is like the 'call this person' note for when something goes wrong.

### Question 79

A new allergy is like a warning label that must be written down and shown to the doctor right away.

### Question 80

A payment plan is like splitting a big purchase into smaller monthly pieces so it is easier to pay.

### Question 81

Sharing private details is like only telling a secret to someone who is allowed to know.

### Question 82

Rescheduling is like moving a meeting to a new day and erasing the old one from the calendar.

### Question 83

If someone suddenly has trouble breathing, you get help right away instead of finishing paperwork.

### Question 84

Recording the reason is like writing down why someone came to see the teacher, in their own words.

### Question 85

If the results are not ready, you honestly say 'not yet' and note that the office will follow up.
